U007: Is answer accuracy sensitive enough to detect version confusion, or is a dedicated temporal-contamination metric required?

Evidence available:
- TempFinRAG: reports answer accuracy AND temporal evidence leakage separately; leakage fell 10.8%→1.7% while accuracy rose 66.7%→78.9%. The fact that leakage is reported separately, and that a verifier checks temporal validity, implies answer accuracy alone did not capture temporal correctness.
- SituatedQA: reports answer accuracy; the 15-point drop is an accuracy effect for present-day questions, and they analyzed failures. But SituatedQA's construction has different answers per context, so accuracy is sensitive there — because answers differ.
- C010 (my inference) states answer accuracy can be insensitive because near-duplicate amended clauses may yield the same answer string.
- Legal NLP survey (2410.21306) — didn't mention metrics.
- Survey p.7: retrieval can fail due to mismatches; retrieval quality is bottleneck — implies retrieval-level metrics matter.
- Also the regulatory RMA benchmark reports ROUGE/BERTScore/faithfulness only — no temporal metric (because no time dimension).
- Fusing Temporal Graphs / Enhancing Temporal Sensitivity: metrics not stated.

So U007 resolution: A dedicated version-level metric is required (or at least strongly advisable) because (a) point-in-time work with genuinely distinct temporal evidence reports a separate leakage metric alongside accuracy, and (b) wording reuse means accuracy can be invariant to which version was retrieved. But it's not that accuracy is useless: when the gold answer differs across versions (as in SituatedQA's context-dependent questions), accuracy is sensitive. So: partially resolved → resolution: use version-level contamination as primary; accuracy as secondary/co-primary only on the stratum where the gold answer actually differs between versions; require a "answer-difference" screen: for each query, verify that the superseded/not-yet-in-force version would yield a different answer than the gold version; only those queries test version selection via accuracy.

That's a concrete, useful design refinement: add an "answer-differential" filter/stratum. This could revise M005 (or add M007). Let me revise M003? The tool created a new id when I passed id=M003. Support: TempFinRAG reports answer accuracy and temporal evidence leakage as separate metrics and a verifier for temporal validity (implying accuracy alone was insufficient to capture temporal correctness); SituatedQA's accuracy effects arise from questions deliberately constructed so that answers differ by temporal context; the RMA regulatory benchmark reports only answer-quality metrics because it has no temporal dimension; the survey identifies retrieval quality as the bottleneck and lists temporal mismatch as a failure mode, none of which answer accuracy directly exposes. input.confidence_basis: Direct evidence that a temporal-correctness metric is reported separately from answer quality in point-in-time work, plus the structural argument that wording reuse can make answers invariant to version. Tempered because accuracy is demonstrably sensitive when the gold answers genuinely differ across temporal contexts (SituatedQA).
input.resolution: Resolved with a design consequence: a version-level metric is required as the primary outcome, but answer accuracy is not useless - it is only sensitive where the gold answer actually differs between versions. Point-in-time financial QA reports answer accuracy and temporal evidence leakage as separate metrics and adds a temporal-validity verifier, which indicates accuracy alone did not capture temporal correctness; the regulatory retrieval benchmark reports only answer-quality metrics but has no temporal dimension at all; and the temporal QA survey treats retrieval quality as the bottleneck and lists temporal mismatch as a failure mode that answer accuracy does not directly expose. Concrete requirement: report version-level contamination (fraction of retrieved/cited passages not in force at the target date) and version confusion as primary, and use answer accuracy as co-primary only on an answer-differential stratum - queries screened so that retrieving the superseded or not-yet-in-force version would produce a different reference answer.

input.description: Define the outcome hierarchy explicitly: (1) primary - version-level temporal contamination and version confusion, computed from retrieved/cited passages and their in-force status at the target date; (2) co-primary on an answer-differential stratum - answer accuracy, evaluated only on queries screened so that the non-gold version yields a different reference answer; (3) diagnostic - retrieval metrics (nDCG/recall) and abstention. Report the fraction of queries passing the answer-differential screen, since it bounds how much of the corpus can be assessed by answer accuracy at all.
input.expected_benefit: Prevents the confound where identical wording across versions masks retrieval errors, while still allowing an end-task claim on the subset of queries where version choice changes the answer. The screen fraction is itself an informative result about how often version confusion matters in practice.
input.experimental_difficulty_basis: Requires generating or annotating a reference answer per candidate version (or an equivalence check between versions) before the answer-differential screen can be applied; then standard accuracy evaluation follows on the surviving subset.
input.implementation_difficulty_basis: Contamination is a rule over passage ids and validity intervals; the screen adds a version-to-answer comparison, which can be automated with a fixed reader and manual spot checks.
input.main_risk: If most query-version pairs fail the answer-differential screen, the end-task claim collapses to a metric-only result, which weakens practical significance even if statistically clean.
input.potential_novelty: Hedged: the contamination idea adapts point-in-time financial QA's leakage metric, but the answer-differential screen (verifying that version choice can change the answer before using accuracy as evidence) was not found in any retrieved work and is a methodological contribution in its own right.
required_baselines: Recency-only ranking with the same outcome hierarchy
Semantic-only ranking with the same outcome hierarchy
input.technical_mechanism: For each query, obtain the reference answer under each candidate version of the relevant clause (using a fixed reader and prompts) and mark the query as answer-differential if the gold version's answer differs from at least one competing version's answer. Compute contamination and version confusion for every query from the retrieved passage set and validity intervals. Evaluate answer accuracy only on the answer-differential subset, and report the screen pass rate separately so metric-only and end-task conclusions are distinguishable.
input.title: Outcome hierarchy with an answer-differential screen for accuracy
input.why_differs: Reviewed temporal benchmarks report answer accuracy (or leakage in finance) as a single outcome; none screens queries for whether version choice can change the answer, so accuracy is used indiscriminately even when wording reuse makes it insensitive. This modification separates version-selection correctness from end-task correctness and reports how often the two can differ.

This modification makes both the version-selection error and the conditions under which it matters part of the measured design.
